abstract: We introduce a quantum algorithm that produces approximate solutions for combinatorial optimization problems. The algorithm depends on an integer $p\geq 1$ and the quality of the approximation improves as $p$ is increased. The quantum circuit that implements the algorithm consists of unitary gates whose locality is at most the locality of the objective function whose optimum is sought. The depth of the circuit grows linearly with $p$ times (at worst) the number of constraints. If $p$ is fixed, that is, independent of the input size, the algorithm makes use of efficient classical preprocessing. If $p$ grows with the input size a different strategy is proposed. We study the algorithm as applied to MaxCut on regular graphs and analyze its performance on 2-regular and 3-regular graphs for fixed $p$. For $p=1$, on 3-regular graphs the quantum algorithm always finds a cut that is at least 0.6924 times the size of the optimal cut.

specification.problem: Approximate MaxCut via a p-layer alternating-operator quantum algorithm (QAOA, as this abstract describes): prepare a parameterized state from a cost unitary and a mixing unitary, choose the angles classically to maximize the expected cut value, then sample a bit string whose cut is close to optimal. The abstract claims a worst-case approximation ratio of 0.6924 for p=1 on 3-regular graphs.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Smallest useful construction (chosen as an assumption since no experiment_scope was supplied): p=1 QAOA for MaxCut on the 4-vertex ring C_4 (2-regular graph, edges (0,1),(1,2),(2,3),(3,0)), using n=4 qubits. Scope covers the cost Hamiltonian, mixer, the single-layer state, the expectation function to be optimized classically, the recalled closed form for a 2-regular ring at p=1, and the abstract's 0.6924 claim as a stated bound. Outside scope: general p>1 layers and their performance scaling, the locality/depth arguments, the 'different strategy' for p growing with input size, the derivation of the 0.6924 bound on 3-regular graphs, and any 3-regular instance.

equations.label: MaxCut cost Hamiltonian
equations.description: Encodes the MaxCut objective as a diagonal 2-local Hamiltonian; each edge term is 1 if the edge is cut and 0 otherwise. Uses Z_j|z\rangle=(-1)^{z_j}|z\rangle.
equations.justification: The abstract names MaxCut as the objective and says gate locality matches objective locality; the standard diagonal encoding of a 2-local MaxCut objective gives exactly this operator.
assumptions: Bit z_j encodes the side of vertex j; qubit j corresponds to vertex j

equations.label: Mixing Hamiltonian
equations.description: Transverse-field mixer; its exponential is a product of single-qubit X rotations.
equations.justification: Standard QAOA mixer recalled from background knowledge; the abstract does not specify it.
assumptions: The algorithm uses the transverse-field mixer rather than a constraint-preserving mixer

equations.label: p-layer QAOA state (p=1 instance)
equations.description: Alternating application of the cost unitary and mixer unitary starting from the uniform superposition. e^{-i\gamma C} factors into m commuting two-qubit ZZ rotations (one per edge), e^{-i\beta B} into n single-qubit X rotations, consistent with depth linear in p times the number of constraints.
equations.justification: Recalled as the known structure of this algorithm (QAOA); the abstract only states dependence on p, locality bounded by the objective's locality, and depth linear in p times the number of constraints, which this product form is consistent with but does not uniquely determine.
assumptions: Operator ordering: rightmost factor acts first; layer l=1 acts first
Exactly one cost and one mixer exponential per layer

equations.label: Expected cut and classical angle optimization
equations.description: The figure of merit is the expectation of C in the variational state; for fixed p the maximizing angles are found by classical preprocessing (for bounded-degree graphs F_p depends only on local subgraph structure and can be evaluated classically).
equations.abstract_quote: If $p$ is fixed, that is, independent of the input size, the algorithm makes use of efficient classical preprocessing.
equations.justification: The abstract states fixed-p classical preprocessing; in QAOA this preprocessing is the classical determination of angles maximizing the expected objective, which is the quantity whose ratio to the optimum is reported.
assumptions: The preprocessing consists of maximizing F_p over angles; the abstract does not describe the procedure

equations.label: p=1 edge expectation on a 2-regular ring (recalled, unverified)
equations.description: Closed form for a single edge of a ring (triangle-free, degree 2) at p=1, obtained from the light-cone of the edge (4 qubits); maximizing gives expected cut 3n/4. For C_4 (even ring, C_max=n=4) this gives ratio 0.75. This is an exact expectation, not a bound; sampled cuts fluctuate around it.
equations.justification: Recalled formula for QAOA p=1 on triangle-free regular graphs specialized to degree 2; not derived from the abstract and not verified here by simulation. The abstract only says 2-regular graphs were analyzed.
assumptions: Ring has n>3 so that the two endpoints of an edge have distinct other neighbours (true for C_4)
Formula recalled from memory; should be checked numerically before use

equations.label: Stated worst-case ratio for p=1 on 3-regular graphs
equations.description: Abstract's performance guarantee; the derivation (case analysis over local edge neighbourhoods) is not given in the abstract and is outside this reconstruction.
equations.abstract_quote: For $p=1$, on 3-regular graphs the quantum algorithm always finds a cut that is at least 0.6924 times the size of the optimal cut.
equations.justification: Directly stated in the abstract; interpreted as a bound on the expected cut value (guaranteeing a sampled string of at least that value exists with nonzero probability, and with repeated sampling one is found with high probability).
assumptions: 'Finds a cut' is interpreted as the expected cut size M_1 being at least 0.6924 C_max

registers.name: q
registers.role: One qubit per vertex of C_4; qubit j holds bit z_j (cut side of vertex j). Basis state |z\rangle = |z_3 z_2 z_1 z_0\rangle with qubit 0 least significant; Z_j|z\rangle=(-1)^{z_j}|z\rangle.

specification.initial_state: |+\rangle^{\otimes 4} = H^{\otimes 4}|0000\rangle, the uniform superposition over all 16 bit strings.

steps.description: Classical preprocessing: for p=1 on the ring instance, evaluate F_1(\gamma,\beta) (via eq_5 or by direct classical computation on the 4-qubit light cone) and pick maximizing angles (\gamma^*,\beta^*)=(\pi/4,\pi/8) (to be verified numerically).
Prepare the uniform superposition by applying H to each of the 4 qubits.

Apply the cost unitary e^{-i\gamma^* C} = \prod_{(j,k)\in E} e^{-i\gamma^*(\mathbb{1}-Z_jZ_k)/2} as four commuting two-qubit ZZ-phase gates on edges (0,1),(1,2),(2,3),(3,0) (the global phase e^{-i\gamma^* m/2} may be dropped).
Apply the mixer unitary e^{-i\beta^* B} = \prod_{j=0}^{3} e^{-i\beta^* X_j} as four single-qubit X rotations R_X(2\beta^*).
Measure all qubits in the computational basis to obtain z; compute C(z) classically; repeat the circuit to estimate F_1 and retain the best observed string.

specification.measurement: Measure all 4 qubits in the computational (Z) basis, yielding a bit string z\in\{0,1\}^4. Each outcome is a candidate cut with value C(z) computed classically from eq_1. Repeating O(m) times (or more) gives an estimate of F_1 and, with high probability, a sample with C(z)\ge F_1 (since C(z) is bounded by m, Chebyshev-type arguments apply).
specification.classical_postprocessing: Compute C(z) for each sampled string; report the maximum observed cut and the sample mean as an estimate of F_1(\gamma^*,\beta^*). For the C_4 instance compare the mean to the recalled value 3 (ratio 3/4 of C_max=4). Angle selection itself is classical preprocessing (eq_4), e.g. a grid search over (\gamma,\beta) using the analytic edge expectation or exact 4-qubit simulation.
assumptions: No experiment_scope was supplied; the instance (C_4 ring, p=1, n=4 qubits) is a choice made here as the smallest useful construction illustrating the 2-regular analysis mentioned in the abstract
The algorithm is identified as QAOA with transverse-field mixer and one cost/mixer pair per layer; the abstract does not spell this out
Qubit j \leftrightarrow vertex j, little-endian bit ordering, Z_j|z\rangle=(-1)^{z_j}|z\rangle
The optimal p=1 angles and the 3/4 ratio for even rings are recalled from background knowledge and are unverified here
The 0.6924 guarantee is interpreted as a bound on the expected cut value for p=1
Cut values are integers; the expected cut F_p is generally a non-integer real number and is not itself a cut
